inheritedFindings.claim: The same label `m.expires` ("Expires" / "만료") carries two different meanings on one screen: on the stage card it renders the frozen TTL constant `${stage.approvalTtlMinutes} min` (always "60 min", even for an `already_exists` stage approved 55 minutes ago), while on the execution card (:503) it renders the real absolute `approvalExpiresAt` timestamp, so the stage row can read as "60 minutes of authority remaining" when almost none is left.
inheritedFindings.reproduction: With a durable stage approved 55 minutes earlier, mount /admin/prompt-refiner-shadow: the stage GET returns `approvalTtlMinutes: 60` (lib/promptRefinerStageAdmission.ts:485, a constant, not a remaining-time value) and `status: "already_exists"`, so the stage card shows Expires = "60 min"; after approving the run, the execution card shows Expires = the real ISO timestamp ~5 minutes in the future. Expected: the stage field is labelled as a TTL (e.g. m.approvalTtl "Approval window") or shows the stage's actual expiry, so one label does not mean two things.

+  stage/run 승인, flag 활성화, 유료 shadow 실행, push·merge·deploy는 이 검토에
+  포함하지 않는다.
